title: Juniper and the Landfall
premise: Sebastian Oyelaran, a bush pilot who has spent fifteen years outrunning a name he buried in the south, agrees to fly dying prospector Elias Vann out of the interior in exchange for a map to the Meridian Star, a wrecked survey vessel rumored to carry unregistered claim-stones worth a fortune. But the map is half of one—the other half belongs to Juniper Vann, Elias's estranged daughter, who arrives demanding answers and a ride. Hunted by the Corvane salvage fleet and by a concession inspector who recognizes Sebastian's old callsign, they must locate the wreck, decide whether to sell it or honor Elias's wish to sink it forever, and beat the fleet's permit clock. In the end Sebastian chooses truth over invisibility: he surrenders his hidden identity to save Juniper from a Corvane trap, they scuttle the claim-stones rather than let them be strip-mined, and the two fly out broke but free as the permits expire behind them.
about_author: Wren Thackeray is the pen name of a former floatplane dispatcher who spent six seasons in remote northern camps before turning to fiction. Their short stories have appeared in several adventure anthologies, and this is their first novel.

chapters.title: Weather Coming Down
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A routine medicine run into the interior goes sideways when fog forces an unplanned landing at a derelict prospecting camp, where Sebastian finds Elias Vann dying of a gut wound. Emotional beat: unease—Sebastian's instinct for invisibility wars with the man bleeding out on the dock.

chapters.title: The Price of a Ride
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Elias offers a hand-drawn map to the Meridian Star wreck in exchange for a promise: get him out alive, or if not, finish what he started. Sebastian takes the map but refuses the promise. Beat: guilt taking root; the wilderness 'forgets nothing' theme introduced.

chapters.title: Juniper
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She lands at Sebastian's airstrip uninvited, having tracked her father's last radio call, carrying the other half of the map and a rifle she clearly knows how to use. Beat: friction and wary mutual assessment; two people who both survive by trusting no one.

chapters.title: Half a Map
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced together by a Corvane spotter plane overhead, they compare fragments and realize neither can find the wreck alone. They strike a temporary alliance. Beat: reluctant partnership; loyalty begins forming where only leverage existed.

chapters.title: Callsign Kestrel
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Concession inspector Marguerite Iles arrives at the strip and greets Sebastian by a name he hasn't heard in fifteen years. She gives him three days before she files her report. Beat: dread; the past stops being past.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the coastal registry office they learn the salvage concession expires in six tides—and that Corvane's lead captain has already filed coordinates that are wrong by miles. Beat: the race clock starts; hope tangled with suspicion about how Elias really got his wound.

chapters.title: The Long Water
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The flight north through storm cells tests the plane and the alliance; Juniper proves herself navigating by dead reckoning when the radio dies. Beat: earned respect; flying as confession—Sebastian tells her a piece of why he disappeared.

chapters.title: What Elias Buried
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Reading her father's journal at a fuel cache, she learns he helped sink the Meridian Star deliberately—to hide evidence of a Corvane atrocity, not treasure. Beat: betrayal and reframing; the 'treasure' may be a liability.

chapters.title: Corvane on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The salvage fleet's tender appears in the same bay; a near-collision and a tense dockside conversation with the fleet's fixer, Dree Halloran, who offers to buy their silence. Beat: temptation; Sebastian recognizes the offer because he once took one like it.

chapters.title: Tide Two
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following the combined map into a maze of channels, they find the first marker—a cairn Elias built—with fresh boot prints beside it. Someone else has the route. Beat: paranoia tightening; trust between them becomes load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Flashback chapter: how Sebastian Oyelaran became someone else after testifying against Corvane's predecessor company and watching witnesses die. Beat: identity theme deepened; invisibility revealed as scar tissue, not strategy.

chapters.title: Iles Catches Up
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Inspector Iles intercepts them at a ranger station, offering immunity for testimony—if Sebastian signs his real name. Juniper sees him almost do it. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made explicit; first real fight between the pair.

chapters.title: Tide Four
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They locate the wreck site beneath a shoal visible only at low tide—but Dree Halloran's dive barge is anchored two coves over, waiting out weather. Beat: claustrophobic tension; the enemy is close enough to hear generators.

chapters.title: Night Dive
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Against all sense, they dive at night on the turning tide and reach the hold, finding not gold but sealed crates of records and sample cores proving Corvane poisoned the watershed. Beat: awe and horror; the truth is heavy and dangerous.

chapters.title: Halloran's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Halloran boards their camp at dawn, reveals she knows Sebastian's true identity, and offers everything—money, erased records, safety—in exchange for the crates. Beat: the dark mirror; Sebastian faces the exact choice that broke him before.

chapters.title: Elias's Promise
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A satellite phone call: Elias survived, barely, in a coastal hospital, and asks Juniper to sink the evidence rather than trade it—because names on paper won't bring back the river. Beat: grief and clarity; Juniper must choose between justice-as-punishment and justice-as-protection.

chapters.title: Tide Five
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Corvane moves early, tipped off by a leak in the registry office; a chase through the channels ends with their plane shot up on a gravel bar. Beat: crisis point; escape routes closing, allies scarce, clock nearly run out.

chapters.title: Kestrel Flies Again
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. To draw Corvane off Juniper and the crates, Sebastian broadcasts openly under his real name, daring the company to make a martyr of him while Iles listens on an open channel. Beat: climax begins; invisibility abandoned, identity weaponized.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With Corvane's fleet chasing Sebastian's decoy flight, Juniper scuttles the crates beneath the wreck in a final dive as the sixth tide turns and the concession expires. Beat: climax resolves; sacrifice without spectacle, honoring Elias's promise.

chapters.title: The Reckoning Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Iles, holding Sebastian's recorded testimony, opens an inquiry; Halloran burns her own orders and vanishes; Corvane's permit lapses with nothing salvaged. Beat: aftermath and vindication—truth costs everything except itself.

chapters.title: Broke and Free
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian patches the plane, signs his name on Iles's affidavit, and waits at the hospital as Elias wakes. Beat: quiet resolution; the promise finally kept, in letter and spirit.

chapters.title: Northbound
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Juniper takes the right-hand seat as they lift off for the interior—not fleeing now, but choosing the country that knows their names. Final beat: memory and identity reconciled; the wilderness forgets less than people do, but it also forgives more.
